The duplication lies in the domain through which BCOR engages the polycomb repressive complex, and relieves repression of its targets. This is the internal tandem duplication's route.

The fusion's own route, which does not run through the polycomb node above. Overexpressing BCOR::CCNB3, or the truncated CCNB3 alone, activates S phase in cultured fibroblasts, so the appended testis-specific cyclin is sufficient for cell cycle entry. The steps between that and the tumour are not established, and the experiment is in a cell line rather than in the tumour's lineage.

nodes.description: A somatic alteration of BCOR, which encodes the BCL6 corepressor. The two common forms are the BCOR::CCNB3 fusion, from a paracentric inversion joining two genes about 10 Mb apart on the X chromosome, and an internal tandem duplication in the last exon of BCOR. Rarer forms include BCOR::MAML3 and ZC3H7B::BCOR. The alterations differ in mechanism but converge on raised BCOR expression, which is the next node.

nodes.description: Strong, diffuse nuclear BCOR protein, present whichever alteration is present. This convergence is both the biological argument for treating the alterations as one entity and the basis of the diagnostic stain: a BCOR immunohistochemical stain is positive across the fusions and the duplication alike. At the transcriptome level the alterations cluster together and apart from Ewing sarcoma and CIC-rearranged sarcoma.

nodes.description: A sarcoma of bone or deep soft tissue, presenting over a wide age range but centred on adolescence for the fusion stratum and on infancy for the duplication stratum. In the 36-case cohort of fusion-positive tumours, ages ran from 2 to 44 with a mean and median of 15, there was a striking male predominance, and locations were slightly more often bone than soft tissue with two renal cases.

nodes.description: BCOR acts genome-wide through polycomb repressive complex 1.1. The internal tandem duplication falls in the exon encoding the domain that binds the complex, and in human neural stem cells it derepressed PRC2-target genes relative to wild-type BCOR. This node carries the mechanism for the duplication specifically; the fusion's own route to transformation runs through the appended cyclin.

nodes.description: Most patients are treated on Ewing sarcoma regimens, and unlike in CIC-rearranged sarcoma the histological response is usually good: seven of nine evaluable cases in one cohort showed more than 60 per cent necrosis in post-therapy resections. No regimen has been developed specifically for this entity and no randomised comparison exists.

nodes.description: About 20 per cent of BCOR::CCNB3 sarcomas are metastatic at diagnosis, and local recurrence after surgery occurs in up to about 20 per cent, which a management review attributes to infiltrative growth. In the multicentre comparison, a low rate of synchronous metastases was one of the features separating BCOR::CCNB3 cases from CIC-rearranged ones. In the 36-case pathology cohort there were 6 local recurrences and 4 distant metastases, to lung, soft tissue or bone, and pancreas.

nodes.description: A cellular tumour spanning round to spindle morphology, with monomorphic nuclei, fine chromatin, a delicate capillary network and variable myxoid or collagenous stroma. The range of morphology is wider than in Ewing sarcoma and is part of why molecular confirmation is needed. In cultured cells, overexpressing the fusion or a truncated CCNB3 activates S phase, which is the one direct link from the fusion to proliferation.
